cards.#1: The Foreman jacket is the anchor of the Ironworks Division, cut from heavyweight stone-washed striped denim with a full metal zip, antique nickel hardware and the Ironworks Division artwork across the back. Everything else in the run is a variation on it. Three hundred and forty-eight dollars.
cards.#2: The Foreman short is the carpenter version, with utility patch pockets throughout, a hammer loop, an engraved metal tack button and a metal zip fly. Two hundred and forty-eight dollars for denim shorts is a number, but these are workwear cut short rather than summer shorts.
cards.#3: These are actual overalls, in medium-weight striped denim with the same stone wash, with adjustable elastic shoulder straps, a multi-compartment bib, a hammer loop and a utility pocket. Nobody needs a pair of golf overalls, and this is the most fun thing Malbon made this year.
cards.#4: The Foreman sweatshirt is an oversized drop-shoulder crewneck in heavyweight cotton jersey with a washed finish and the Ironworks artwork across the chest. It is the piece from the capsule you would wear on a day with no golf in it. Malbon list it as a preorder shipping 26 August.
cards.#5: The snapback comes in the same striped stone-washed denim as the jacket, five panels with a flat brim and a structured crown, with Ironworks Division embroidery on the front. At fifty-eight dollars it is the cheapest way into the capsule.
cards.#6: The driver cover is black stone-washed striped denim, padded and soft-lined, with embroidered Division branding. Headcovers are where a capsule like this either lands or falls apart, and a hundred and twenty-eight dollars puts this one on the right side of that.
cards.#7: The Vista is the plain entry point to the line: relaxed cotton with a functional chest pocket and the Ironworks graphic on the front. The pocket is the detail that keeps it from being a plain tee. Sixty-eight dollars, and the one piece here that will go unnoticed away from the course.
cards.#8: The Grounds is solid cotton on one face and contrasting plaid on the other, collarless and open-fronted with chore pockets and snap cuffs. Two jackets for three hundred and forty-eight dollars, and it wears as a shirt jacket rather than a coat. Malbon list it as a preorder shipping 26 August.
cards.#9: The Ridge comes from Malbon’s Icons line in nylon and spandex, a quarter-zip with a drawcord hood and waist on lock stoppers and two zip pockets. It is the plainest thing in the collection and probably the one you would wear most. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars.
cards.#10: The Horizon is a quarter-zip rebuilt as a chambray rugby, in cotton-polyester with a stand collar and an adjustable bungee hem on cord locks. The colour block across the chest is doing most of the work. A hundred and ninety-eight dollars.
cards.#11: The Station Shirt is stone-washed cotton herringbone twill with dual chest patch pockets and engraved Malbon snaps behind a hidden placket. It reads as military workwear filtered through a golf brand, and the brown is the better of the two colourways. Two hundred and twenty-eight dollars.
cards.#12: The same shirt runs in olive, with a straight hem and a relaxed fit through the body. It pairs with the Station Pant in the same herringbone if you want to commit to the whole look, and the straight hem means it can be worn out. Two hundred and twenty-eight dollars.
cards.#13: The Benchmark is soft washed cotton chambray with oversized utility chest pockets, contrast decorative stitching and engraved Malbon buttons. It is the lightest layer in the collection and the one you can wear open over a tee. A hundred and ninety-eight dollars.
cards.#14: The Hickory Windshirt is midweight hickory stripe with an antique nickel YKK quarter-zip, dual chest patch pockets and a drawcord hem. Malbon cut it short-sleeved, which is a strange decision and a good one. Two hundred and twenty-eight dollars.
cards.#15: The Inkwash windshirt is nylon and elastane with mesh-lined back ventilation, invisible on-seam zip pockets and a silicone zipper pull. The print is the only loud thing Malbon did this season, and the indigo is the version that works. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars.
cards.#16: The same windshirt comes in olive, with the same venting and the same drawcord hem. Between the two colourways and the matching short, the Inkwash print carries four pieces in the collection. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars.
cards.#17: The Fairway is heavyweight cotton pique, overdyed, with contrast white stitching at the sleeves and hem and tonal embroidery. The overdye is what gives it a lived-in look before you have worn it in. A hundred and forty-eight dollars.
cards.#18: The Brickwork is enzyme-washed open-knit cotton with a ribbed hem and cuffs and a full-needle placket. The texture is the point, and it reads as a knit shirt rather than a golf polo. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars.
cards.#19: The Brickwork also comes in washed black, with the same open knit and the same ribbed trims. Washed black is softer than flat black and harder to place as golf clothing, which is presumably the idea. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars.
cards.#20: The Crosscut is cotton and cashmere in an engineered pointelle knit with a full button front. The knit is where the money went, and it is the most expensive-feeling piece in the collection that is not a shoe. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars, with no logo doing any of the work.
cards.#21: The cream Crosscut has ribbed sleeve cuffs and branding you have to look for, in a knit fine enough that it does not read as a polo at all. A hundred and seventy-eight dollars, and the piece to keep on for dinner afterwards.
cards.#22: The Station Pant is the same stone-washed cotton herringbone twill as the shirt, mid-rise and relaxed through the leg. Malbon’s own spec sheet calls the cloth Army herringbone, and buying the pant with the shirt is the whole look. Two hundred and twenty-eight dollars.
cards.#23: The olive pant is wide and pleated, cropped short enough to show the shoe. Given the Red Wing oxford at the end of the collection, the crop is probably deliberate. Two hundred and twenty-eight dollars, and the pleats are what separate it from a chino.
cards.#24: The Scooter is lightweight stretch nylon, mesh-lined, with an elastic waist over an internal drawcord, dual zip back welt pockets and a five-inch inseam. It is the one technical bottom in the collection, and it carries the Inkwash print. A hundred and forty-eight dollars.
cards.#25: Malbon and Red Wing have rebuilt the Shop Moc Oxford for the course, in full-grain oiled Oro Legacy leather tanned at Red Wing’s own S.B. Foot Tanning Company. It has a classic moc toe, a Goodyear welt and a Traction Tred outsole, and the welt means it can be resoled, which almost no golf shoe can claim. Four hundred dollars and the best object in the collection.
cards.#26: Malbon made this with CLUCT, the Tokyo streetwear label, carrying artwork by Kaji of Joytown Tattoo Studio. It is handcrafted in Japan from brass under a thick sterling silver coating. Seventy-eight dollars for a divot tool is absurd, and this one comes close to justifying it.
cards.#27: The Station Snapback is stone-washed herringbone twill with a custom woven front label, five panels and a flat brim. It is the quiet alternative to the Ironworks cap, in the same cloth as the Station shirt and pant. Forty-eight dollars.

kickers.1: Malbon put a name on it this season. Ironworks Division is a run of heavyweight stone-washed striped denim in hickory stripe, the cloth painters and railroad workers wore, with antique nickel hardware and hammer loops. It is the most committed thing in the collection.
kickers.2: Three layers here handle a cold morning, and the reversible flannel is the interesting one. Solid cotton on one face and contrasting plaid on the other, collarless and open-fronted so it works as a shirt jacket rather than a coat.
kickers.3: The Station Shirt is stone-washed cotton herringbone twill with engraved snap closures, in brown and in olive. The Inkwash windshirt is the technical end of the collection, in nylon and elastane with mesh-lined back venting and a print that repeats on the shorts.
kickers.4: There are no logos to speak of in this group. The Crosscut is a cotton-cashmere pointelle knit with a full button front and the Brickwork is an enzyme-washed open knit. The Fairway comes in overdyed heavyweight pique with contrast white stitching.
kickers.5: The Station Pant is the same stone-washed herringbone as the shirt, and the lookbook is clearly encouraging you to buy both. The Scooter is the technical outlier in the group.
kickers.6: The two best pieces in the collection are both made by somebody else. One is a Red Wing oxford on a Goodyear welt and the other is a divot tool from CLUCT in Tokyo.
